market_context.summary: Friday 2026-11-20 was a correlated liquidation, not a rotation. SPY closed 689.81 (-3.64%) on 151.4M shares against a 52.2M 30-day average (2.9x) and finished at 689.81 against a session low of 686.75 — on the low, with no reversal bid; QQQ closed 608.45 (-5.67%) and sits 20.24% off its 45-day high against SPY's 11.75%. The tell is that GLD fell 3.67% on the same day: in a growth scare gold rises, so gold, equities and crypto falling together while only Treasuries rose (TLT +1.37% on 1.7x volume) is a deleveraging event, correlated assets sold to raise cash. Credit did not crack — HYG only -0.26% — which supports the deleveraging read and contradicts a solvency repricing. The regime behind it is a discount-rate shock with a dated trigger: Kalshi's KXFEDDECISION-26DEC order books price a 25bp Fed HIKE at ~89% for the 2026-12-09 FOMC against fed funds effective at 3.88%, with US10Y at 5.04% and the 10y-2y at +0.29 — ~116bp of term premium above the funds rate, which is a fiscal/term-premium regime, not a duration-friendly easing one. The open book is 13 longs into that, and five of fifteen positions sit under 1.4 ATR from their stops (XLV 0.32, DKS 0.48, HUN 0.69, RTX 0.71, ADM 1.16, XLU 1.39). That is the honest headline of this report, not any single new idea. Sunday run: US equities and futures are closed, every equity/ETF figure here is the Friday 2026-11-20 official close and all equity entries are for the Monday 2026-11-23 open. Crypto is live and bouncing — BTC $60,810 (+5.16%/24h) but still -29.6% off its 60-day high, the whole complex up 2.8-5.3% together, which is one beta bounce rather than nine signals.

catalyst.action: HOLD and ADD A STOP AT 238.5. Do not add to the position — it is 7% above the entry zone, which is for reference. Trim a third at 339.76.

recommendations.thesis: Amendment that fixes a hole rather than changing a view. HII has been held since 2026-10-12 as a swing position with no stop, which config/strategy.md permits only for long_term ideas — a swing thesis with unbounded downside is not a risk-controlled position, it is a hope with a target attached. Setting the stop at 238.5 puts it exactly 2.0 ATR below the 262.0 entry on an ATR14 of 11.7463, which is the floor for a stock, and the trade still clears reward-to-risk comfortably at (339.76-262.0)/(262.0-238.5) = 3.31. The position is +7.0% and the stop sits 41.84 below the market, 3.56 ATR of room, so nothing is being tightened onto the price.
recommendations.key_risk: The stop is 15% below the last close, so it bounds the tail without protecting the gain — HII can give back the entire 7% and more before 238.5 is reached. That is the honest cost of setting a stop at a level wide enough to be a real risk control rather than a level chosen to feel safe. Shipbuilding is also a single-customer business: a continuing resolution or a programme deferral moves it more than anything in the price chart, and the book already holds RTX in the same sector.
recommendations.counter_argument: The case against adding a stop at all is that HII is a multi-decade Navy shipbuilding backlog — arguably a long_term holding, in which case no stop is required and an invalidation condition would do instead. That is a fair reading and would be defensible if the position had been opened that way, but it was opened on a 39-day swing horizon with a chart target of 339.76, and reclassifying a position to long_term after it has moved in your favour is how a losing swing becomes an investment. If the thesis is genuinely long_term it should be re-opened as one, with a valuation anchor rather than a 339.76 level.

recommendations.thesis: CVS closed Friday at 80.84, which is 9.7x the $8.33 of EPS it has actually reported over the last four quarters (2.09 + 2.58 + 2.57 + 1.09, each a fetched actual), and 26.96% below its own 150-day high of 110.68. Against that de-rating the operating record has gone the other way: it has beaten consensus in four of the last four quarters and the analyst recommendation trend is improving, with bullish share at 87.5%, up 2.7 points. That combination — a cheapening multiple against beating numbers — is the de-rated-but-not-broken case, and the target of 101.5 is 12.2x the same trailing EPS, still 8.3% below where the stock traded within the last 150 days.
recommendations.key_risk: Managed care has a genuinely fat left tail: if the medical cost trend re-accelerates, EPS does not fall 10% but 20-25%, and a 9x multiple on $6.50 is roughly 58 — far below the 71.5 stop. The stop is what bounds that, and it will not be honoured in a gap. This is also a sector the open book is already heavy in via XLV and ABT, so treat it as the third position on one driver and do not add a fourth.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that 9.7x is not a discount but an accurate price for a business whose earnings quality is deteriorating — pharmacy reimbursement compressing and insurance underwriting worsening — in which case the trailing $8.33 is the peak and the multiple is cheap on a number that is about to fall. The reason I do not accept it as the base case is the beat record: four consecutive quarters of actuals coming in above estimates is the opposite of what a company sliding into negative revisions prints, and analysts have been revising toward the stock, not away. If the next print breaks that streak, the thesis is void regardless of price. RED TEAM: a third objection is answered nowhere above. 28 of 32 analysts are already buy or strong-buy (87.5%, and rising 2.7 points), so de-rated-but-not-broken is the consensus read, not a differentiated one — which is why the 'positioning' evidence cannot pay for conviction 4: it is crowding cited as confirmation. Being right about a view seven analysts in eight already hold earns very little. And the 101.5 target is a 25.6% / 5.5 ATR re-rating with no dated catalyst, by the catalyst field's own admission, inside a 15-session horizon.

That is leadership rather than a falling knife, which is the distinction this report has most often got wrong. recommendations.key_risk: Verizon is one of the most indebted large caps in the market and the Fed is 89% priced to hike on 2026-12-09, which raises refinancing cost and makes the dividend compete against a 5.04% 10-year — the single clearest argument against owning it here. The earnings record is also only adequate: 2 beats of the last 4 quarters, materially weaker than the 4-of-4 behind the CVS idea, which is why the entry is scaled rather than taken at once.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that defensive low-beta names outperform in the first leg of a drawdown and then catch up on the way down, so a month of relative strength is a lagging statistic rather than a signal — and that a telecom at 9.3x is permanently cheap for good reason, being a capital-intensive business in a three-way price war with no growth. The reason I still take it is that the relative strength is not one month of noise: VZ beats SPY and XLC across 1, 3 and 6 months, which is a persistent pattern rather than a defensive flinch, and the 9.2x entry multiple limits what further de-rating looks like. RED TEAM: the objection named in key_risk — an 89%-priced 25bp hike on 2026-12-09, inside this holding period, on one of the most indebted large caps in the market — is NOT answered above; the counter_argument answers a different one. The answer this report gives TLT (a hike this telegraphed is already in a 5.04% 10-year, so what moves things is the statement's growth read rather than the move) would serve here and was never made. Left standing, it is why conviction is 3 and not 4. The record is also weaker than 'only adequate': the two most recent quarters both MISSED, at -0.08% and -0.22%.

It closed 25.39 above its 24.71 SMA20, only 3.37% off its 45-day high and 16.68% above the range low, in a week when SPY fell 3.64% and QQQ 5.67% on Friday alone. A packaged-food name holding near its high through a liquidation is the defensive bid doing what it is supposed to do.

Staples are also a crowded hiding place: if the deleveraging reaches the point of selling what still works, KHC is exactly what gets sold, and the 21.2 stop is 16.5% below the market, so it would give back the entire gain before protecting anything. RED TEAM, numerically: from the filled 25.39 the position is 2.70 from target and 4.19 from stop — a forward ratio of 0.64:1 and a forward break-even of 60.8%. The defence left standing for the expectancy flag was precisely that the entry-derived 26.1% baseline is the wrong frame for a filled position; taken seriously, that frame makes the claimed 48% BELOW a coin flip rather than 22 points above one. If the market stabilises after the Dec 9 FOMC, the rotation reverses and KHC gives back 10% faster than it gained it, with the target never reached. That is a real risk and the reason the recommendation is to trim into strength rather than to hold for the full target.

recommendations.thesis: Amendment to the open position, levels unchanged, and the reason to keep it is the opposite of the obvious one. The instinct on discovering that a 25bp hike is 89% priced is to sell duration — but a hike that well telegraphed is already in a 5.04% 10-year, and what TLT actually traded on Friday 2026-11-20 was flight to quality: +1.37% on 66.1M shares against a ~38M average while SPY fell 3.64%, GLD fell 3.67% and the Nasdaq 100 had its worst week since 2020. recommendations.key_risk: TLT is long duration in a tape where the stated worry is persistent inflation, and that is the one regime in which it loses while equities also lose — the 2022 correlation, where the hedge fails exactly when needed. recommendations.counter_argument: Friday's bid may be the mechanical end of a deleveraging rather than a view: Treasuries are the collateral of choice, so forced sellers of gold and equities park proceeds there for days, not quarters. If that is all it was, TLT gives the 1.37% back as soon as the margin calls clear, and with fed funds heading to roughly 4.13% against a 5.04% 10-year there is no cutting cycle underneath to carry it to 84.3.
